# Adjudication Task — Chapter 486

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃486화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“잠깐 이야기 좀 할까?”
  6|
  7|“싫다. 꺼져라.”
  8|
  9|“그렇군.”
 10|
 11|한 치의 망설임도 없이 가까워지는 적천강의 모습에, 문경의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
 12|
 13|“싫다고 했을 텐데.”
 14|
 15|“들었다. 그래서?”
 16|
 17|“역시 말이 안 통하는군. 나이는 뒷구멍으로 먹었나?”
 18|
 19|“어린놈이 어르신한테 못하는 말이 없구나. 노부가 네놈보다 족히 예닐곱 살은 더 먹었느니라.”
 20|
 21|“도대체 나이가 몇 살이길래 그런…….”
 22|
 23|“허벅지 살이다. 이 대가리에 피도 안 마른 어린놈아.”
 24|
 25|“참으로 개 같은…… 됐다. 말을 말아야지.”
 26|
 27|순간 울컥했던 문경은 고개를 절레절레 저었다.
 28|
 29|겉모습은 젊다 못해 어려 보이는 소년이지만 그 역시 장장 백여 년의 인생을 걸어온 노인.
 30|
 31|하지만 적천강과 대화를 하고 있다 보면 평정심을 잃은 어린애가 되는 기분이었다.
 32|
 33|‘사람 열 받게 하는 데에는 도가 텄군. 스승이나 제자나 아주 쏙 빼닮았어.’
 34|
 35|적천강과 진태경. 이 두 사람이라면 세 치 혓바닥으로 누군가의 울화통을 터트려 죽일 수 있을 것도 같았다.
 36|
 37|그에 비하면 지금쯤 사천에서 병자들을 돌보고 있을 늙은 제자는 부처의 환생이나 다름없었다.
 38|
 39|‘보고 싶구나. 잘 지내고 있느냐?’
 40|
 41|문경이 자신의 착한 제자를 그리워하는 사이. 휘적거리는 팔자걸음으로 다가온 적천강이 바위에 걸터앉았다.
 42|
 43|“뭘 보고 있었나?”
 44|
 45|“그걸 대답해 줘야 할 이유는 없지.”
 46|
 47|“나쁘지 않은 선택이야. 그럼 날이 밝을 때까지 이러고 있자고. 늙은이 둘이서 오붓하게.”
 48|
 49|“하나는 알고 둘은 모르는군. 떠나면 그만이다.”
 50|
 51|“둘은 알고 셋은 모르나 본데, 노부가 오늘만 이럴 것 같나?”
 52|
 53|“……!”
 54|
 55|“오늘, 내일, 모레. 글피. 안 그래도 늙으니 잠이 없어져서 적적했는데, 이것도 나쁘지 않겠군.”
 56|
 57|돌아서려던 문경의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다. 파르르 떨리는 눈꺼풀로 적천강을 바라보던 그가 탄식하듯 중얼거렸다.
 58|
 59|“악랄한 늙은이 같으니.”
 60|
 61|“흠. 이제사 겨우 대화를 나눌 준비가 된 모양이로군.”
 62|
 63|“……찾아온 용건을 말해라.”
 64|
 65|“이야기가 좀 길어질 수도 있을 것 같은데.”
 66|
 67|“최대한 짧게.”
 68|
 69|“최대한 짧게라.”
 70|
 71|새카맣게 물든 강물을 바라보던 적천강이 한마디를 툭, 내뱉었다.
 72|
 73|“앞으로 그놈, 잘 봐줘.”
 74|
 75|“뭐?”
 76|
 77|잠시 미간을 좁혔던 문경이 입을 열었다.
 78|
 79|“그놈이라면, 진태경?”
 80|
 81|“그래. 진태경 그놈 말고 또 누가 있나?”
 82|
 83|“그걸 왜 나한테 부탁하는 거지?”
 84|
 85|“글쎄. 잘 모르겠군.”
 86|
 87|적천강은 문득 고개를 들어 하늘을 바라보았다.
 88|
 89|휘영청 떠 있는 보름달. 닿을 수 없는 그곳으로부터 쏟아진 빛이 유난히도 환하다.
 90|
 91|“갑자기 그런 생각이 들었어. 노부가 언제까지 그놈과 함께할 수 있을까 하는, 그런 생각.”
 92|
 93|일백 년의 세월, 참으로 길었다.
 94|
 95|강산은 변했고 왕조(王朝)가 뒤바뀌었다. 그리고…… 어린 소년은 백발의 노인이 되었다.
 96|
 97|적천강을 물끄러미 바라보던 문경이 나직하게 뇌까렸다.
 98|
 99|“늙었군.”
100|
101|“그래. 늙어 버렸어.”
102|
103|세월의 흐름에 따라 늙고 해진 것은 몸뚱어리뿐만이 아니다. 보이지 않는 감정과 마음 역시 천천히 마모되어 닳아 없어진다.
104|
105|어느 순간 문득 죽음을 떠올렸을 때, 누군가의 곁에 얼마나 더 오래 머무를 수 있을까 생각했을 때 사람은 늙었다는 사실을 깨닫는다.
106|
107|바로 지금의 적천강처럼.
108|
109|그리고 문경은 현재 적천강의 마음을 누구보다 잘 이해할 수 있는 유일한 사람이었다.
110|
111|“심마(心魔)가 찾아왔나?”
112|
113|“심마라, 오래됐지.”
114|
115|적천강은 자조 섞인 웃음을 흘렸다.
116|
117|자식처럼 키웠으나 살귀(殺鬼)로 자라난 옛 제자가 떠난 후부터, 그의 마음엔 진한 먹구름이 드리워져 있었다.
118|
119|그리고 그때 느꼈던 슬픔과 죄책감은 수십여 년간 족쇄처럼 적천강의 심신을 옥죄었다.
120|
121|어느 날 갑자기 나타난, 진태경이라는 빛이 내리쬐기 전까지.
122|
123|“이제는 아픈 과거야. 그저 기억할 뿐, 고통스럽지는 않은.”
124|
125|“그렇다면 왜?”
126|
127|“초조해졌으니까.”
128|
129|심마라는 놈은 형태가 정해져 있는 것이 아니다. 마음을 어지럽히고 깨달음을 방해하는 장애물.
130|
131|지금 적천강을 사로잡은 심마는 초조함이라는 감정이었다.
132|
133|“이십 년, 아니 십 년만 더 일찍 그 녀석을 만났다면 좋았을 텐데…… 너무 늦어 버렸어.”
134|
135|적천강은 손을 들어 달을 가렸다. 자신과 달리 조금도 늙지 않은 저 환한 달빛이 주름진 얼굴을 비추는 것이 싫었다.
136|
137|“예전 같지 않아. 몸도, 마음도. 그나마 지금까지 버틸 수 있었던 것도 녀석이 있었기에 가능했던 게지.”
138|
139|구화산(九華山)에서 보낸 일 년 동안 성장한 것은 진태경만이 아니었다.
140|
141|적천강 역시 가르침을 통해 약간의 깨달음을 얻었고, 그 덕분에 가파르게 달려가던 노환의 발걸음을 붙잡을 수 있었다.
142|
143|하지만.
144|
145|“이미 알고 있었잖나. 노부의 선천지기(先天眞氣)가 상했다는 것을.”
146|
147|선천지기, 혹은 진원진기(眞元眞氣)라 불리는 기운은 인체를 이루는 모든 것의 원천이자 생명력, 그 자체다.
148|
149|하남에서의 일을 떠올린 적천강의 입가에 씁쓸한 미소가 맺혔다.
150|
151|“후회하진 않네. 그 아이를 살리기 위해서라면 뭐든 했을 테니까.”
152|
153|적천강의 말은 진심이었다. 열 번, 백 번을 다시 돌아간다 해도 그는 같은 선택을 했을 것이다. 그만큼 당시의 상황은 절박했다.
154|
155|생명력이나 다름없는 선천지기를 끌어올려 부족한 공력을 대신할 만큼.
156|
157|그렇게 한때나마 혈주를 죽음의 문턱까지 끌어당겼던 화신귀무(火神鬼舞)에는, 자신의 생명력을 장작으로 불태운 늙은 스승의 결의가 깃들어 있었다.
158|
159|“충분히 각오했던 일이었어. 설령 살아난다 해도 예전 같지는 않으리라 짐작했지.”
160|
161|말없이 적천강을 바라보던 문경이 나직한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
162|
163|“그랬을 거다. 그 녀석이 구해 온 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)이 아니었다면.”
164|
165|“그래, 모두 천운이었지. 그 아이가 자네를 찾아낸 것도.”
166|
167|그러나 두 사람은 알고 있었다.
168|
169|희대의 영약인 천년설삼과 의술이 하늘에 닿았다는 신의의 치료로도 적천강의 선천지기를 되돌릴 수는 없다는 것을.
170|
171|이 모든 것은 임시방편에 불과하다.
172|
173|커다란 바위로 무너진 둑을 틀어막는다고 해도, 둑 안에 갇혀 있던 물줄기는 작은 빈틈을 통해 천천히 조금씩, 그리고 쉼 없이 흘러나오고 있었다.
174|
175|“그것 때문에 나를 찾아온 건가? 그 녀석을 부탁하려고?”
176|
177|“글쎄, 어떨 것 같나?”
178|
179|되묻는 적천강을 보며 작게 혀를 찬 문경이 말을 이었다.
180|
181|“늙어서 그런지 걱정도 많아졌군. 그런 고민은 몇 년 뒤에 해도 늦지 않는다.”
182|
183|사람마다 품은 기운의 크기도, 그릇도 다르다.
184|
185|평범한 양민이나 삼류 무인이 작은 개울이라면, 적천강은 끝없이 펼쳐진 바다였다.
186|
187|계속되는 선천지기의 소실로 인해 천천히 힘을 잃겠지만, 이미 적천강의 몸 상태를 파악하고 있는 문경이 보기에 그의 걱정은 이른 감이 없지 않았다.
188|
189|“노부의 몸이니 익히 알고 있네. 적어도 오늘 당장 죽지는 않겠지.”
190|
191|“그러니 허튼 생각 그만하고 돌아가. 차라리 이 시간에 그 녀석을 붙잡고 한 수라도 더 가르치는 것이 나을 테니.”
192|
193|“하지만 내일 무슨 일이 벌어질지는 모르는 일이지.”
194|
195|“뭐?”
196|
197|“선천지기가 조금씩 사라져서, 어느 날 갑자기 급사할까 봐 찾아온 거라 생각하나?”
198|
199|미간을 좁히는 문경을 응시하며, 적천강이 천천히 말을 이었다.
200|
201|“느껴져. 점차 쇠약해지고 있다는 것이. 이미 정마대전 때도 느끼지 못했던 죽을 고비를 여러 번 넘겼지. 이런 노부가 앞으로도 이어질 숱한 전투에서 버틸 수 있을지는…… 저 하늘 위에서 지켜보고 있을 빌어먹을 누군가만 알고 있겠지.”
202|
203|“……!”
204|
205|“굉도, 그 친구가 그런 말을 한 적이 있네. 천기(天氣)가 어그러지고, 정마대전 때보다 거대한 환란이 다가오고 있다고.”
206|
207|법왕 굉도의 예측은 현실로 이루어졌다.
208|
209|불과 일 년 뒤, 무림의 태산북두인 소림이 피와 시체로 뒤덮였고, 술과 고기를 좋아하던 현명한 고승은 죽음을 맞이했다.
210|
211|어느덧 암천이라는 먹구름은 하남과 사천, 호북에까지 드리워졌다.
212|
213|그리고 적천강은 알 수 있었다. 저 먹구름이, 곧 머지않아 천하를 뒤덮으리라는 것을.
214|
215|“이보게, 살성.”
216|
217|문경을 바라보는 적천강의 눈빛에 짙은 회한이 묻어 나왔다.
218|
219|“알 수 없는 일들이 벌어지고 있네. 우리가 알고 있던 모든 것이 무너지고 있어.”
220|
221|세인들은 흔히들 무림을 장강에 빗대어 말하고는 한다.
222|
223|장강후랑추전랑(長江後浪推前浪). 장강의 뒷물결이 앞 물결을 밀어 낸다는 말이 있는 것도 그 때문이다.
224|
225|그러나 지금 암천이 천하 곳곳에서 벌이고 있는 일들과 기이한 현상들은…… 장강이 아니라 하늘과 땅을 뒤엎는 역천(逆天)과도 같았다.
226|
227|적천강과 문경. 장장 일백여 년의 세월을 살아온 두 노인이 알고 있던 모든 법칙은 산산이 부서져 무너지고 있었다.
228|
229|‘만약 진태경. 그 아이가 한 말이 사실이라면 더더욱. 아니, 아니지. 그럴 리 없어. 아니어야 한다.’
230|
231|적천강은 순간 뇌리에 스치는 생각을 애써 털어냈다.
232|
233|진태경이 늘 그랬던 것처럼 농담처럼 던진 실없는 헛소리일 뿐이다.
234|
235|정확히는 그렇게 믿고 싶었다.
236|
237|이미 몸과 마음이 늙고 마모된 적천강은 아직 그러한 충격적인 이야기를 받아들일 준비가 되지 않았다.
238|
239|“어쨌건 노파심에 부탁하는 거야. 이 지랄 같은 무림에서는 무슨 일이 벌어져도 이상하지 않으니까. 노부처럼 나날이 쇠약해지는 늙은이 하나 죽는다 한들, 그리 놀라운 일은 아니지.”
240|
241|문경은 묘한 눈빛으로 적천강을 응시했다.
242|
243|화왕(火王)이라 불리는 거인은 오늘따라 유독 작아 보였고, 언제 찾아올지 모르는 죽음을 입에 올리는 담담한 목소리는 유난히도 귓가에 맴돌았다.
244|
245|‘부탁. 부탁이라.’
246|
247|바로 그 화왕의 입에서 나온 단어라고는 믿어지지 않을 정도다.
248|
249|천천히 몸을 일으키는 적천강을 말없이 바라보던 문경이 내심 중얼거렸다.
250|
251|‘이런, 나도 늙었군.’
252|
253|비록 몸은 어려졌지만, 마음은 낡았다.
254|
255|오랜 세월 비 한 방울 내리지 않던 마음 한구석이 축축하게 젖어드는 것은 그러한 이유 때문일 것이다.
256|
257|“……후.”
258|
259|문경이 작게 한숨을 내쉰 그때, 무거운 엉덩이를 뗀 적천강은 이미 손을 흔들며 돌아서고 있었다.
260|
261|“이만 가 보지. 달구경 잘하게.”
262|
263|“뭐?”
264|
265|이게 무슨 소린가.
266|
267|잠시 뇌정지가 온 문경이 가까스로 입을 열었다.
268|
269|“간다니?”
270|

“Do you think I came because I’m afraid my innate qi will slowly disappear until I suddenly drop dead one day?”

[P100]
Jeok Cheongang stared at Mungyeong’s furrowed brow and continued slowly.

[P101]
“I can feel it. I’m growing weaker. I’ve already survived several brushes with death unlike anything I faced even during the Great Faction War. Whether an old man like me can endure all the battles still to come… only some damned bastard watching from the heavens knows.”

[P102]
“…!”

[P103]
“Hong Dao once told me that the heavenly patterns were becoming distorted, and a calamity greater than the Great Faction War was approaching.”

[P104]
Dharma King Hong Dao’s prediction had become reality.

[P105]
Only a year later, Shaolin—the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim—had been covered in blood and corpses, and the wise high monk who loved alcohol and meat had met his death.

[P106]
Now the dark cloud called Dark Heaven had spread across Henan, Sichuan, and Hubei.

[P107]
And Jeok Cheongang knew that before long, it would cover the entire world.

[P108]
“Listen, Slaughter Saint.”

[P109]
Deep regret filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes as he looked at Mungyeong.

[P110]
“Things we cannot understand are happening. Everything we knew is collapsing.”

[P111]
People often compared the Murim to the Yangtze.

[P112]
*The waves behind on the Yangtze push the waves ahead.* That was why the saying existed.

[P113]
But the strange phenomena and events Dark Heaven was causing throughout the world were nothing like the Yangtze. They were an act of defying heaven itself, overturning heaven and earth.

[P114]
Everything Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong had known, every law they had understood over more than a century of life, was shattering around them.

[P115]
*All the more so if what Jin Taekyung said was true. No. No, that can’t be. It mustn’t be.*

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang forced the thought from his mind.

[P117]
It was only another ridiculous piece of nonsense Taekyung had tossed out like a joke, as he always did.

[P118]
More precisely, that was what Jeok Cheongang wanted to believe.

[P119]
His body and heart had already grown old and worn. He was not yet ready to accept such a shocking story.

[P120]
“Anyway, I’m only asking to put my mind at ease. Anything can happen in this goddamn Murim. It would hardly be surprising if one old man growing weaker by the day were to die.”

[P121]
Mungyeong regarded Jeok Cheongang with an inscrutable look.

[P122]
The giant known as the Fire King seemed unusually small tonight, and his calm voice as he spoke of a death that could come at any moment lingered in Mungyeong’s ears.

[P123]
*A favor. He asked me for a favor.*

[P124]
It was hard to believe those words had come from the Fire King himself.

[P125]
Mungyeong silently watched Jeok Cheongang rise to his feet.

[P126]
*Damn. I’ve grown old too.*

[P127]
Though his body had grown young, his heart was old.

[P128]
That must have been why one corner of his heart, untouched by even a drop of rain for so many years, was slowly growing damp.

[P129]
“…Hah.”

[P130]
Just as Mungyeong let out a quiet sigh, Jeok Cheongang hauled his heavy backside off the rock and turned away with a wave.

[P131]
“I’ll be going. Enjoy the moon.”

[P132]
“What?”

[P133]
What was he talking about?

[P134]
Mungyeong’s mind briefly stopped working. He barely managed to speak.

[P135]
“You’re leaving?”

[P136]
“Of course. Shouldn’t you be grateful that this nuisance is leaving?”

[P137]
“I haven’t answered you yet.”

[P138]
“What do you mean? I believe I’ve already heard your answer.”

[P139]
“Wait. What are you—”

[P140]
“I heard you loud and clear, young friend.”

[P141]
“No, what kind of crazy old bastard—”

[P142]
His composure, which rarely ever broke, came crashing down.

[P143]
Mungyeong stared incredulously at Jeok Cheongang’s retreating back and shouted.

[P144]
“What do you expect me to do?”

[P145]
“Teach him a few things. The mindset he’ll need, for example. And if any of your secret martial arts might be useful, slip him a manual.”

[P146]
“Secret martial arts? A manual?”

[P147]
For a moment, Mungyeong doubted his own ears.

[P148]
An individual’s or sect’s secret martial arts were the crystallized essence of everything they had learned. They could not be taught even for ten thousand pieces of gold and were more precious than life itself.

[P149]
Yet Jeok Cheongang was telling him to teach those secret arts to someone else’s Disciple.

[P150]
Mungyeong asked with complete sincerity.

[P151]
“…Have you gone senile and forgotten what secret martial arts are?”

[P152]
“I know exactly what they are. Unless you plan on saving them to wipe your ass with, teach him a few.”

[P153]
“You lunatic.”

[P154]
“You don’t have anyone else to teach them to anyway. Let your old Disciple in Sichuan keep saving lives, and teach our boy how to kill properly.”

[P155]
Was that something he could say with a straight face?

[P156]
Mungyeong was too dumbfounded to speak. Meanwhile, having said everything he wanted to say, Jeok Cheongang was already speeding away into the distance.

[P157]
*Whoosh!*

[P158]
“What a… fucking mess.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 486

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃486화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“잠깐 이야기 좀 할까?”
  6|
  7|“싫다. 꺼져라.”
  8|
  9|“그렇군.”
 10|
 11|한 치의 망설임도 없이 가까워지는 적천강의 모습에, 문경의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
 12|
 13|“싫다고 했을 텐데.”
 14|
 15|“들었다. 그래서?”
 16|
 17|“역시 말이 안 통하는군. 나이는 뒷구멍으로 먹었나?”
 18|
 19|“어린놈이 어르신한테 못하는 말이 없구나. 노부가 네놈보다 족히 예닐곱 살은 더 먹었느니라.”
 20|
 21|“도대체 나이가 몇 살이길래 그런…….”
 22|
 23|“허벅지 살이다. 이 대가리에 피도 안 마른 어린놈아.”
 24|
 25|“참으로 개 같은…… 됐다. 말을 말아야지.”
 26|
 27|순간 울컥했던 문경은 고개를 절레절레 저었다.
 28|
 29|겉모습은 젊다 못해 어려 보이는 소년이지만 그 역시 장장 백여 년의 인생을 걸어온 노인.
 30|
 31|하지만 적천강과 대화를 하고 있다 보면 평정심을 잃은 어린애가 되는 기분이었다.
 32|
 33|‘사람 열 받게 하는 데에는 도가 텄군. 스승이나 제자나 아주 쏙 빼닮았어.’
 34|
 35|적천강과 진태경. 이 두 사람이라면 세 치 혓바닥으로 누군가의 울화통을 터트려 죽일 수 있을 것도 같았다.
 36|
 37|그에 비하면 지금쯤 사천에서 병자들을 돌보고 있을 늙은 제자는 부처의 환생이나 다름없었다.
 38|
 39|‘보고 싶구나. 잘 지내고 있느냐?’
 40|
 41|문경이 자신의 착한 제자를 그리워하는 사이. 휘적거리는 팔자걸음으로 다가온 적천강이 바위에 걸터앉았다.
 42|
 43|“뭘 보고 있었나?”
 44|
 45|“그걸 대답해 줘야 할 이유는 없지.”
 46|
 47|“나쁘지 않은 선택이야. 그럼 날이 밝을 때까지 이러고 있자고. 늙은이 둘이서 오붓하게.”
 48|
 49|“하나는 알고 둘은 모르는군. 떠나면 그만이다.”
 50|
 51|“둘은 알고 셋은 모르나 본데, 노부가 오늘만 이럴 것 같나?”
 52|
 53|“……!”
 54|
 55|“오늘, 내일, 모레. 글피. 안 그래도 늙으니 잠이 없어져서 적적했는데, 이것도 나쁘지 않겠군.”
 56|
 57|돌아서려던 문경의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다. 파르르 떨리는 눈꺼풀로 적천강을 바라보던 그가 탄식하듯 중얼거렸다.
 58|
 59|“악랄한 늙은이 같으니.”
 60|
 61|“흠. 이제사 겨우 대화를 나눌 준비가 된 모양이로군.”
 62|
 63|“……찾아온 용건을 말해라.”
 64|
 65|“이야기가 좀 길어질 수도 있을 것 같은데.”
 66|
 67|“최대한 짧게.”
 68|
 69|“최대한 짧게라.”
 70|
 71|새카맣게 물든 강물을 바라보던 적천강이 한마디를 툭, 내뱉었다.
 72|
 73|“앞으로 그놈, 잘 봐줘.”
 74|
 75|“뭐?”
 76|
 77|잠시 미간을 좁혔던 문경이 입을 열었다.
 78|
 79|“그놈이라면, 진태경?”
 80|
 81|“그래. 진태경 그놈 말고 또 누가 있나?”
 82|
 83|“그걸 왜 나한테 부탁하는 거지?”
 84|
 85|“글쎄. 잘 모르겠군.”
 86|
 87|적천강은 문득 고개를 들어 하늘을 바라보았다.
 88|
 89|휘영청 떠 있는 보름달. 닿을 수 없는 그곳으로부터 쏟아진 빛이 유난히도 환하다.
 90|
 91|“갑자기 그런 생각이 들었어. 노부가 언제까지 그놈과 함께할 수 있을까 하는, 그런 생각.”
 92|
 93|일백 년의 세월, 참으로 길었다.
 94|
 95|강산은 변했고 왕조(王朝)가 뒤바뀌었다. 그리고…… 어린 소년은 백발의 노인이 되었다.
 96|
 97|적천강을 물끄러미 바라보던 문경이 나직하게 뇌까렸다.
 98|
 99|“늙었군.”
100|
101|“그래. 늙어 버렸어.”
102|
103|세월의 흐름에 따라 늙고 해진 것은 몸뚱어리뿐만이 아니다. 보이지 않는 감정과 마음 역시 천천히 마모되어 닳아 없어진다.
104|
105|어느 순간 문득 죽음을 떠올렸을 때, 누군가의 곁에 얼마나 더 오래 머무를 수 있을까 생각했을 때 사람은 늙었다는 사실을 깨닫는다.
106|
107|바로 지금의 적천강처럼.
108|
109|그리고 문경은 현재 적천강의 마음을 누구보다 잘 이해할 수 있는 유일한 사람이었다.
110|
111|“심마(心魔)가 찾아왔나?”
112|
113|“심마라, 오래됐지.”
114|
115|적천강은 자조 섞인 웃음을 흘렸다.
116|
117|자식처럼 키웠으나 살귀(殺鬼)로 자라난 옛 제자가 떠난 후부터, 그의 마음엔 진한 먹구름이 드리워져 있었다.
118|
119|그리고 그때 느꼈던 슬픔과 죄책감은 수십여 년간 족쇄처럼 적천강의 심신을 옥죄었다.
120|
121|어느 날 갑자기 나타난, 진태경이라는 빛이 내리쬐기 전까지.
122|
123|“이제는 아픈 과거야. 그저 기억할 뿐, 고통스럽지는 않은.”
124|
125|“그렇다면 왜?”
126|
127|“초조해졌으니까.”
128|
129|심마라는 놈은 형태가 정해져 있는 것이 아니다. 마음을 어지럽히고 깨달음을 방해하는 장애물.
130|
131|지금 적천강을 사로잡은 심마는 초조함이라는 감정이었다.
132|
133|“이십 년, 아니 십 년만 더 일찍 그 녀석을 만났다면 좋았을 텐데…… 너무 늦어 버렸어.”
134|
135|적천강은 손을 들어 달을 가렸다. 자신과 달리 조금도 늙지 않은 저 환한 달빛이 주름진 얼굴을 비추는 것이 싫었다.
136|
137|“예전 같지 않아. 몸도, 마음도. 그나마 지금까지 버틸 수 있었던 것도 녀석이 있었기에 가능했던 게지.”
138|
139|구화산(九華山)에서 보낸 일 년 동안 성장한 것은 진태경만이 아니었다.
140|
141|적천강 역시 가르침을 통해 약간의 깨달음을 얻었고, 그 덕분에 가파르게 달려가던 노환의 발걸음을 붙잡을 수 있었다.
142|
143|하지만.
144|
145|“이미 알고 있었잖나. 노부의 선천지기(先天眞氣)가 상했다는 것을.”
146|
147|선천지기, 혹은 진원진기(眞元眞氣)라 불리는 기운은 인체를 이루는 모든 것의 원천이자 생명력, 그 자체다.
148|
149|하남에서의 일을 떠올린 적천강의 입가에 씁쓸한 미소가 맺혔다.
150|
151|“후회하진 않네. 그 아이를 살리기 위해서라면 뭐든 했을 테니까.”
152|
153|적천강의 말은 진심이었다. 열 번, 백 번을 다시 돌아간다 해도 그는 같은 선택을 했을 것이다. 그만큼 당시의 상황은 절박했다.
154|
155|생명력이나 다름없는 선천지기를 끌어올려 부족한 공력을 대신할 만큼.
156|
157|그렇게 한때나마 혈주를 죽음의 문턱까지 끌어당겼던 화신귀무(火神鬼舞)에는, 자신의 생명력을 장작으로 불태운 늙은 스승의 결의가 깃들어 있었다.
158|
159|“충분히 각오했던 일이었어. 설령 살아난다 해도 예전 같지는 않으리라 짐작했지.”
160|
161|말없이 적천강을 바라보던 문경이 나직한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
162|
163|“그랬을 거다. 그 녀석이 구해 온 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)이 아니었다면.”
164|
165|“그래, 모두 천운이었지. 그 아이가 자네를 찾아낸 것도.”
166|
167|그러나 두 사람은 알고 있었다.
168|
169|희대의 영약인 천년설삼과 의술이 하늘에 닿았다는 신의의 치료로도 적천강의 선천지기를 되돌릴 수는 없다는 것을.
170|
171|이 모든 것은 임시방편에 불과하다.
172|
173|커다란 바위로 무너진 둑을 틀어막는다고 해도, 둑 안에 갇혀 있던 물줄기는 작은 빈틈을 통해 천천히 조금씩, 그리고 쉼 없이 흘러나오고 있었다.
174|
175|“그것 때문에 나를 찾아온 건가? 그 녀석을 부탁하려고?”
176|
177|“글쎄, 어떨 것 같나?”
178|
179|되묻는 적천강을 보며 작게 혀를 찬 문경이 말을 이었다.
180|
181|“늙어서 그런지 걱정도 많아졌군. 그런 고민은 몇 년 뒤에 해도 늦지 않는다.”
182|
183|사람마다 품은 기운의 크기도, 그릇도 다르다.
184|
185|평범한 양민이나 삼류 무인이 작은 개울이라면, 적천강은 끝없이 펼쳐진 바다였다.
186|
187|계속되는 선천지기의 소실로 인해 천천히 힘을 잃겠지만, 이미 적천강의 몸 상태를 파악하고 있는 문경이 보기에 그의 걱정은 이른 감이 없지 않았다.
188|
189|“노부의 몸이니 익히 알고 있네. 적어도 오늘 당장 죽지는 않겠지.”
190|
191|“그러니 허튼 생각 그만하고 돌아가. 차라리 이 시간에 그 녀석을 붙잡고 한 수라도 더 가르치는 것이 나을 테니.”
192|
193|“하지만 내일 무슨 일이 벌어질지는 모르는 일이지.”
194|
195|“뭐?”
196|
197|“선천지기가 조금씩 사라져서, 어느 날 갑자기 급사할까 봐 찾아온 거라 생각하나?”
198|
199|미간을 좁히는 문경을 응시하며, 적천강이 천천히 말을 이었다.
200|
201|“느껴져. 점차 쇠약해지고 있다는 것이. 이미 정마대전 때도 느끼지 못했던 죽을 고비를 여러 번 넘겼지. 이런 노부가 앞으로도 이어질 숱한 전투에서 버틸 수 있을지는…… 저 하늘 위에서 지켜보고 있을 빌어먹을 누군가만 알고 있겠지.”
202|
203|“……!”
204|
205|“굉도, 그 친구가 그런 말을 한 적이 있네. 천기(天氣)가 어그러지고, 정마대전 때보다 거대한 환란이 다가오고 있다고.”
206|
207|법왕 굉도의 예측은 현실로 이루어졌다.
208|
209|불과 일 년 뒤, 무림의 태산북두인 소림이 피와 시체로 뒤덮였고, 술과 고기를 좋아하던 현명한 고승은 죽음을 맞이했다.
210|
211|어느덧 암천이라는 먹구름은 하남과 사천, 호북에까지 드리워졌다.
212|

[P30]
“You vicious old bastard.”

[P31]
“Hm. Looks like you’re finally ready to talk.”

[P32]
“…Tell me why you came.”

[P33]
“This might take a while.”

[P34]
“Make it as short as possible.”

[P35]
“‘As short as possible,’ huh?”

[P36]
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the river, its waters dyed pitch-black, and tossed out a single sentence.

[P37]
“Look after that brat from now on.”

[P38]
“What?”

[P39]
Mungyeong frowned for a moment before speaking.

[P40]
“By ‘that brat,’ you mean Jin Taekyung?”

[P41]
“Yes. Who else would I mean?”

[P42]
“Why are you asking me?”

[P43]
“Who knows? I’m not sure myself.”

[P44]
Jeok Cheongang suddenly raised his head toward the sky.

[P45]
A full moon hung brilliantly overhead. Light poured from that unreachable place, unusually bright.

[P46]
“I suddenly found myself wondering how long I’d be able to stay with that brat.”

[P47]
A hundred years was a very long time.

[P48]
Mountains and rivers had changed. Dynasties had risen and fallen. And… a young boy had become a white-haired old man.

[P49]
Mungyeong gazed at Jeok Cheongang and murmured quietly.

[P50]
“You’ve grown old.”

[P51]
“Yes. I have.”

[P52]
It was not only the body that grew old and worn with the passage of time. Unseen feelings and the heart itself were slowly weathered away.

[P53]
A person realized they had grown old when death suddenly came to mind, or when they wondered how much longer they could remain beside someone.

[P54]
Just as Jeok Cheongang was doing now.

[P55]
And Mungyeong was the one person who understood Jeok Cheongang’s feelings better than anyone.

[P56]
“Has the Heart Demon come calling?”

[P57]
“The Heart Demon? That came a long time ago.”

[P58]
Jeok Cheongang let out a self-deprecating laugh.

[P59]
Ever since the former Disciple he had raised like a son became the Killing Ghost and left him, a dark cloud had hung over his heart.

[P60]
The grief and guilt he had felt then had shackled Jeok Cheongang’s body and mind for decades.

[P61]
Until a light called Jin Taekyung suddenly appeared and shone down upon him.

[P62]
“It’s a painful memory now. I remember it, but it no longer hurts.”

[P63]
“Then why?”

[P64]
“Because I’ve grown anxious.”

[P65]
The Heart Demon had no fixed form. It was any obstacle that disturbed the heart and hindered enlightenment.

[P66]
The Heart Demon gripping Jeok Cheongang now was anxiety.

[P67]
“I wish I’d met that boy twenty years earlier. No, even ten years earlier would have been enough… But I met him too late.”

[P68]
Jeok Cheongang raised a hand to cover the moon. He hated how its bright light—unaged, unlike him—shone upon his wrinkled face.

[P69]
“I’m not what I used to be. Neither my body nor my heart. The only reason I’ve endured this long is because that boy was there.”

[P70]
Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had grown during the year they spent on Mount Jiuhua.

[P71]
Through teaching Taekyung, Jeok Cheongang had also gained a measure of enlightenment. Thanks to that, he had managed to slow the rapid advance of his infirmities of old age.

[P72]
But—

[P73]
“You already knew, didn’t you? My innate qi was damaged.”

[P74]
Innate qi, also called true-origin qi, was the source of everything that made up the human body. It was life force itself.

[P75]
Remembering what had happened in Henan, Jeok Cheongang smiled bitterly.

[P76]
“I don’t regret it. I would have done anything to save that boy.”

[P77]
He meant every word. Even if he could go back ten times or a hundred, he would make the same choice. The situation had been that desperate.

[P78]
Desperate enough for him to draw upon the innate qi that was practically his life force to make up for his insufficient internal energy.

[P79]
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon, which had once dragged the Blood Lord to the brink of death, carried the resolve of an old Master who had burned his own life force as fuel.

[P80]
“I was prepared for it. Even if I survived, I knew I would never be the same.”

[P81]
Mungyeong watched him in silence before replying in a low voice.

[P82]
“You wouldn’t have been, if not for the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng that boy brought back.”

[P83]
“Yes. It was all a stroke of heaven-sent fortune. Even the fact that he found you.”

[P84]
But both men knew the truth.

[P85]
Not even the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, an elixir seldom seen in any age, combined with the treatment of the Divine Physician, whose medical skill was said to reach the heavens, could restore Jeok Cheongang’s innate qi.

[P86]
All of it was merely a stopgap.

[P87]
Even if a massive boulder blocked the breach in a collapsed dam, the water trapped behind it would keep seeping through the smallest gap—slowly, little by little, without pause.

[P88]
“Is that why you came to me? To ask me to look after him?”

[P89]
“Who knows? What do you think?”

[P90]
Mungyeong clicked his tongue softly.

[P91]
“You’ve grown more fretful with age. It wouldn’t be too late to worry about that a few years from now.”

[P92]
Every person possessed a different amount of qi and a different vessel to contain it.

[P93]
If an ordinary commoner or Third Rate martial artist was a small stream, Jeok Cheongang was an endless sea.

[P94]
He would slowly lose strength as his innate qi continued to drain away, but Mungyeong already understood the condition of Jeok Cheongang’s body. As far as he could tell, these concerns were premature.

[P95]
“This is my body. I know it well. At least I won’t die today.”

[P96]
“Then stop thinking such foolish thoughts and go back. You’d be better off spending this time teaching that brat one more move.”

[P97]
“But no one knows what might happen tomorrow.”

[P98]
“What?”

[P99]
“Do you think I came because I’m afraid my innate qi will slowly disappear until I suddenly drop dead one day?”

[P100]
Jeok Cheongang stared at Mungyeong’s furrowed brow and continued slowly.

[P101]
“I can feel it. I’m growing weaker. I’ve already survived several brushes with death unlike anything I faced even during the Great Faction War. Whether an old man like me can endure all the battles still to come… only some damned bastard watching from the heavens knows.”

[P102]
“…!”

[P103]
“Hong Dao once told me that the heavenly patterns were becoming distorted, and a calamity greater than the Great Faction War was approaching.”

[P104]
Dharma King Hong Dao’s prediction had become reality.

[P105]
Only a year later, Shaolin—the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim—had been covered in blood and corpses, and the wise high monk who loved alcohol and meat had met his death.

[P106]
Now the dark cloud called Dark Heaven had spread across Henan, Sichuan, and Hubei.

[P107]
And Jeok Cheongang knew that before long, it would cover the entire world.

[P108]
“Listen, Slaughter Saint.”

[P109]
Deep regret filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes as he looked at Mungyeong.

[P110]
“Things we cannot understand are happening. Everything we knew is collapsing.”

[P111]
People often compared the Murim to the Yangtze.

[P112]
*The waves behind on the Yangtze push the waves ahead.* That was why the saying existed.

[P113]
But the strange phenomena and events Dark Heaven was causing throughout the world were nothing like the Yangtze. They were an act of defying heaven itself, overturning heaven and earth.

[P114]
Everything Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong had known, every law they had understood over more than a century of life, was shattering around them.

[P115]
*All the more so if what Jin Taekyung said was true. No. No, that can’t be. It mustn’t be.*

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang forced the thought from his mind.

[P117]
It was only another ridiculous piece of nonsense Taekyung had tossed out like a joke, as he always did.

[P118]
More precisely, that was what Jeok Cheongang wanted to believe.

[P119]
His body and heart had already grown old and worn. He was not yet ready to accept such a shocking story.

[P120]
“Anyway, I’m only asking to put my mind at ease. Anything can happen in this goddamn Murim. It would hardly be surprising if one old man growing weaker by the day were to die.”

[P121]
Mungyeong regarded Jeok Cheongang with an inscrutable look.

[P122]
The giant known as the Fire King seemed unusually small tonight, and his calm voice as he spoke of a death that could come at any moment lingered in Mungyeong’s ears.

[P123]
*A favor. He asked me for a favor.*

[P124]
It was hard to believe those words had come from the Fire King himself.

[P125]
Mungyeong silently watched Jeok Cheongang rise to his feet.

[P126]
*Damn. I’ve grown old too.*

[P127]
Though his body had grown young, his heart was old.

[P128]
That must have been why one corner of his heart, untouched by even a drop of rain for so many years, was slowly growing damp.

[P129]
“…Hah.”

[P130]
Just as Mungyeong let out a quiet sigh, Jeok Cheongang hauled his heavy backside off the rock and turned away with a wave.

[P131]
“I’ll be going. Enjoy the moon.”

[P132]
“What?”

[P133]
What was he talking about?

[P134]
Mungyeong’s mind briefly stopped working. He barely managed to speak.

[P135]
“You’re leaving?”

[P136]
“Of course. Shouldn’t you be grateful that this nuisance is leaving?”

[P137]
“I haven’t answered you yet.”

[P138]
“What do you mean? I believe I’ve already heard your answer.”

[P139]
“Wait. What are you—”

[P140]
“I heard you loud and clear, young friend.”

[P141]
“No, what kind of crazy old bastard—”

[P142]
His composure, which rarely ever broke, came crashing down.

[P143]
Mungyeong stared incredulously at Jeok Cheongang’s retreating back and shouted.

[P144]
“What do you expect me to do?”

[P145]
“Teach him a few things. The mindset he’ll need, for example. And if any of your secret martial arts might be useful, slip him a manual.”

[P146]
“Secret martial arts? A manual?”

[P147]
For a moment, Mungyeong doubted his own ears.

[P148]
An individual’s or sect’s secret martial arts were the crystallized essence of everything they had learned. They could not be taught even for ten thousand pieces of gold and were more precious than life itself.

[P149]
Yet Jeok Cheongang was telling him to teach those secret arts to someone else’s Disciple.

[P150]
Mungyeong asked with complete sincerity.

[P151]
“…Have you gone senile and forgotten what secret martial arts are?”

[P152]
“I know exactly what they are. Unless you plan on saving them to wipe your ass with, teach him a few.”

[P153]
“You lunatic.”

[P154]
“You don’t have anyone else to teach them to anyway. Let your old Disciple in Sichuan keep saving lives, and teach our boy how to kill properly.”

[P155]
Was that something he could say with a straight face?

[P156]
Mungyeong was too dumbfounded to speak. Meanwhile, having said everything he wanted to say, Jeok Cheongang was already speeding away into the distance.

[P157]
*Whoosh!*

[P158]
“What a… fucking mess.”
